roadmap.goal: Story 6389 (FE1): enforce the frontend layer import boundaries in the Vitest suite. Fallow (exact-pinned dev dependency) reads Lighthouse.Frontend/.fallowrc.json (seven root-anchored zones, five forbidden directions) and src/layerBoundaries.enforcement.test.ts compares its findings both ways with the frozen 21-entry allow-list: a new leak fails naming file and import, a fixed leak still listed fails until its entry is deleted. Behaviour-free: no src production file changes, the 21 existing leaks are frozen, not fixed. DISTILL is the canonical author of the test file; DELIVER unskips scenarios and makes them green with the dependency and the config.

phases.name: FE1-1: Fallow and the components -> pages rule

steps.name: Walking skeleton: Fallow installed, zones configured, components leaks compared both ways
steps.description: Read /storage/repos/Lighthouse/.claude/worktrees/velvety-floating-fog/docs/ci-learnings.md (frontend section) first and pre-apply its rules. Install `fallow` as an exact-pinned devDependency (3.36.0, at least 24 h old under pnpm 12's minimum release age; no caret or tilde) with pnpm in Lighthouse.Frontend, so package.json and pnpm-lock.yaml change. Create Lighthouse.Frontend/.fallowrc.json with all seven root-anchored zones (components, context, hooks, models, pages, services, utils) and only the components -> pages rule (the other four rules are FE1-2). Unskip walking-skeleton #1 in the enforcement test. This is the first execution of the test's findLeaks helper: a failure that is BROKEN (cannot resolve fallow, exit 2) rather than RED is a test or setup bug to fix before any RED is trusted; do not rewrite the scenario's intent. Before relying on #17 later, confirm here that `fallow/bin/fallow` resolves through the installed package and that a missing config exits 2 with JSON on stdout naming the config path. Cut note: the DISTILL table puts 10 scenarios (#3-#11, #17) in the rest of FE1-1, over the 8-scenario cap, so they are split into 01-02 and 01-03. No src production file changes. The slice ends with `pnpm build` (runs `biome check --write` + tsc + vite) and `pnpm test` green in Lighthouse.Frontend; check git status afterwards for files biome rewrote.
criteria: The enforcement test runs the installed Fallow (its launcher resolves through the package) and gets a result

With only the components -> pages rule configured, the twelve src/components entries of the allow-list are found, no more and no fewer, so the two-way comparison reports no newcomers and no stale entries
fallow is pinned to an exact version in package.json, with no range prefix
No file under Lighthouse.Frontend/src other than the enforcement test changes
`pnpm exec tsc -b`, `pnpm build` and `pnpm test` pass in Lighthouse.Frontend
steps.scenario_name: the frontend layers > today's leaks > lets components reach into pages only in the twelve listed places, and in all of them

steps.name: A new component-to-page import is refused; test files and repeated imports behave
steps.description: Read /storage/repos/Lighthouse/.claude/worktrees/velvety-floating-fog/docs/ci-learnings.md (frontend section) first. Unskip scenarios #3-#6 (four scenarios: #3 new leak refused, #4 and #5 the .test.ts / .test.tsx importer, #6 one report per file pair). They go BROKEN-then-RED only if setup is wrong; once 01-01 is in place the components rule already exists, so they should go green on unskip: if one does not, fix the config or the helper, not the scenario's intent. #4 and #5 pin that the production-only run excludes test files; #6 pins Fallow's one-edge-per-file-pair behaviour. Also confirm, by hand or a temporary check that is not committed, that a stray sandbox copy of a leaking component (e.g. a copy under `.stryker-tmp/`) is not reported by the check, so no ignorePatterns is needed; if it is reported, add the narrowest ignore to .fallowrc.json and say so in the commit body. No src production file changes. The slice ends with `pnpm build` (runs `biome check --write` + tsc + vite) and `pnpm test` green in Lighthouse.Frontend.
criteria: A component importing a page is reported as exactly one new leak, naming the component and the page
A .test.ts or .test.tsx file under src/components that imports a page is not reported; the control leak still is
A component importing the same page in three ways (two imports and a re-export) is reported once

A stray copy of a leaking component under a sandbox directory such as .stryker-tmp is not reported; evidence (the command run and the Fallow output) is quoted in the step's commit body, and the copy is removed before committing
No file under Lighthouse.Frontend/src other than the enforcement test changes (checked with `git status` after `pnpm build`, whose Biome pass may rewrite files)
`pnpm build` and `pnpm test` pass in Lighthouse.Frontend
steps.scenario_name: the frontend layers > a component reaching into a page > is refused as a new leak, naming the component and the page; the frontend layers > a component reaching into a page > is not reported when it is only a .test.ts file that does so; the frontend layers > a component reaching into a page > is not reported when it is only a .test.tsx file that does so; the frontend layers > a component reaching into a page > is reported once, however many times the component imports that page

steps.name: Stale and duplicate entries are refused; allowed directions are silent; a check that cannot run fails loudly
steps.description: Read /storage/repos/Lighthouse/.claude/worktrees/velvety-floating-fog/docs/ci-learnings.md (frontend section) first. Unskip scenarios #7-#11 and #17 (six scenarios). #7, #8 and #17 are guards that are green on arrival (they protect the counted comparison and the exit-status check; there is no production code to make them red), so unskip the positive scenario work from 01-02 first, then these; #9, #10 and #11 need the components rule and should be green on unskip. #9 proves a fixed leak that is still listed is reported stale by name; #10 and #11 prove the rule is silent for components using hooks and pages using components, with the control leak as the only entry; #17 proves findLeaks throws quoting Fallow's output when the config is missing (status 2 and the config path) instead of returning no leaks. Add the frontend bullet for the components rule to ARCHITECTURE.md at the repo root (section 12, frontend): the layer rule in plain language, where the allow-list and `.fallowrc.json` live, and that a fixed leak must also be deleted from the list. Keep it to the one rule that exists in this slice (FE1-2 extends it to five). No src production file changes. The slice ends with `pnpm build` (runs `biome check --write` + tsc + vite) and `pnpm test` green in Lighthouse.Frontend.
criteria: Finding the same leak twice while it is listed once is refused as a new leak
Listing a leak twice while it is found only once is refused as stale
A listed leak whose import has been removed is refused as stale, naming the entry, until the entry is deleted
A component using a hook and a page using a component are not reported; only the control leak appears
When the boundary check cannot run (missing config), the test fails with a message that quotes what Fallow printed, never an empty leak list
ARCHITECTURE.md section 12 describes the components -> pages rule and where its allow-list lives
No file under Lighthouse.Frontend/src other than the enforcement test changes (checked with `git status` after `pnpm build`, whose Biome pass may rewrite files)
`pnpm build` and `pnpm test` pass in Lighthouse.Frontend
steps.scenario_name: the frontend layers > a leak that is listed once > is refused as a new leak when the same entry turns up a second time; the frontend layers > a leak that is listed once > is refused as stale when it is listed twice but found only once; the frontend layers > a listed leak that has been fixed > is refused as stale until its entry is deleted, naming the entry; the frontend layers > directions the layers allow > report nothing for a component using a hook; the frontend layers > directions the layers allow > report nothing for a page using a component; the frontend layers > a boundary check that cannot run > fails the test, quoting what it printed, instead of reporting no leaks

phases.name: FE1-2: the other four rules and the whole 21-entry list

steps.name: Hooks, services, models and utils rules in force; whole 21-entry list compared both ways
steps.description: Read /storage/repos/Lighthouse/.claude/worktrees/velvety-floating-fog/docs/ci-learnings.md (frontend section) first. Add the other four rules to Lighthouse.Frontend/.fallowrc.json: hooks must not import pages or components, services must not import hooks, models must not import pages, utils must not import services (per the DESIGN zone allow-lists). Unskip #12-#16 (the five-row 'each remaining layer rule is in force' table, one rule per row: BROKEN-free, RED until its rule is added, GREEN after) and #2 (whole frontend, twenty-one entries). Expected small test-file adjustment, intent unchanged: the FE1-1 walking skeleton #1 compares through `leaksUnder("components", ...)`; with all five rules in force the comparison switches to the whole list, and #2 is that whole-list comparison, and #1 stays as the components-scoped skeleton the DISTILL table names (decided at roadmap review); do not remove or merge it. Extend the ARCHITECTURE.md section 12 bullet from the one rule to all five. No src production file changes: the 21 leaks stay frozen. The timing gate is the orchestrator's, not this step's (see the phase descriptions). The slice ends with `pnpm build` (runs `biome check --write` + tsc + vite) and `pnpm test` green in Lighthouse.Frontend.
criteria: A hook importing a page, a hook importing a component, a service importing a hook, a model importing a page and a utility importing a service are each reported as one new leak naming both ends
The whole frontend crosses its layers only in the twenty-one listed places, and in all of them: no newcomers and no stale entries
No file under Lighthouse.Frontend/src other than the enforcement test changes (checked with `git status` after `pnpm build`, whose Biome pass may rewrite files); the 21 leaks remain
ARCHITECTURE.md section 12 describes all five layer rules
Walking skeleton #1 stays as the components-scoped stage (its twelve entries compared both ways); #2 adds the whole-list comparison beside it
`pnpm build` and `pnpm test` pass in Lighthouse.Frontend
